correctness.rationale: The finite-nilpotent S³={0}, S²≠{0}, directed nonzero product relation, and bipartite underlying support are essential. If the target has no length-two directed walk, every source digraph without one maps by source/sink coloring to any target arc, and the directed two-arc path is the unique three-vertex critical obstruction, hence b(D)=3. If p→q→r is in the bipartite target, H_(2m+1) with alternately directed path edges and closing arc has odd underlying cycle, fails any two-coloring target map, but each vertex deletion admits a map to p→q→r; this is an infinite family of critical obstructions, so no finite duality. Published 2026 nilpotent-semiring equivalence then gives finite/nonfinite basis; its stated variable bound max(4,b) gives 4. In the five-element examples all products except ab=bc=z (and optionally ac=z) vanish and z annihilates, hence associativity; the transitive tournament T3 admits exactly digraphs with no directed three-walk, so b=4. Independently checked both 5-element tables for every triple and small directed homomorphisms. Small checks do not replace the unbounded odd-cycle proof or cited correspondence.
